ἀπό.sd: "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative)
ἀπό.kj: (X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with
ἀπό.as:
ἀπό (on the freq. neglect of elision bef. vowels, v. Tdf., Pr., 94, WH, App., 146),
prep. c. gen. (WM, 462 ff.; on its relation to ἐκ, παρά, ὑπό, WM, 456 f.),
[in LXX for מִן, בְּ, לְ;]
from (i.e. from the exterior).
1. Of separation and cessation;
(1) of motion from a place: Mt 5:29, 307:23, Lk 5:222:41, al.;
(2) in partitive sense (M, Pr., 72, 102, 245; MM, s.v.; Bl., § 40, 2), Mt 9:1627:21, Jo 21:10, Ac 5:2, al.; also after verbs of eating, etc.;
(3) of alienation (cl. gen. of separation), after such verbs as λούω (Deiss., BS, 227), λύω, σώζω, παύω, etc.; ἀνάθεμα ἀ., Ro 9:3; ἀποθνήσκειν ἀ., Col 2:20; σαλευθῆναι, II Th 2:2, καθαρός, -ίζειν, ἀ. (Deiss., BS, 196, 216), Ac 20:26, II Co 7:1, He 9:14;
(4) of position, Mt 23:3424:31, al.; after μακράν, Mt 8:30; transposed before measures of distance, Jo 10:1821:8, Re 14:20 (Abbott, JG, 227);
(5) of time, ἀπὸ τ. ὥρας, ἡμέρας, etc., Mt 9:22, Jo 19:27, Ac 20:18, Phl 1:5, al.; ἀπ’ αἰῶνος, Lk 1:70, al.; ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, etc., Mt 19:4, Ro 1:20; ἀπὸ βρέφους, II Ti 3:15; ἀφ’ ἧς, since, Lk 7:45, al.; ἀπὸ τ. νῦν, Lk 1:48, al.; ἀπὸ τότε, Mt 4:17, al.; ἀπὸ πέρυσι, a year ago, II Co 8:109:2; ἀπὸ πρωΐ, Ac 28:23;
(6) of order or rank, ἀπὸ διετοῦς, Mt 2:16; ἀπὸ Ἀβραάμ, Mt 1:17; ἕβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδάμ, Ju 14; ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου, Ac 8:10, He 8:11; ἄρχεσθαι ἀπό, Mt 20:8, Jo 8:9, Ac 8:35, al.
2. Of origin;
(1) of birth, extraction, and hence, in late writers,
(a) of local extraction (cl. ἐξ; Abbott, JG, 227 ff.), Mt 21:11, Mk 15:43, Jo 1:45, Ac 10:38, al.; οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας (WM, § 66, 6; M, Pr., 237; Westc, Rendall, in l.), He 13:24;
(b) of membership in a community or society (Bl., § 40, 2), Ac 12:1, al.;
(c) of material (= cl. gen.; Bl., § 40, 2; M, Pr., 102), Mt 3:427:21;
(d) after verbs of asking, seeking, etc., Lk 11:50, 51, I Th 2:6 (Milligan, in l.);
(2) of the cause, instrument, means or occasion (freq. = ὑπό, παρά, and after verbs of learning, hearing, knowing, etc.; Bl., § 40, 3), Mt 7:1611:29, Lk 22:45, Ac 2:224:369:1312:14, I Co 11:23, Ga 3:2, al.; ἀπὸ τ. ὄχλου, Lk 19:3 (cf. Jo 21:6, Ac 22:11); ἀπὸ τ. φόβου, Mt 14:26, al. (cf. Mt 10:2813:44).
3. Noteworthy Hellenistic phrases: φοβεῖσθαι ἀπό (M, Pr., 102, 107); προσέχειν ἀπό (M, Pr., 102, 107; Milligan, NTD, 50); ἀπὸ νότου (Heb. מִנֶּגֶב), Re 21:13; ἀπὸ προσώπου (מִפְּנֵי), II Th 1:9 (Bl., § 40, 9); ἀπὸ τ. καρδιῶν (בְּלֵב), Mt 18:35; ἀπὸ ὁ ὤν (WM, § 10, 2; M, Pr., 9), Re 1:4.
4. In composition, ἀπό denotes separation, departure, origin, etc. (ἀπολύω, ἀπέρχομαι, ἀπογράφω); it also has a perfective force (M, Pr., 112, 247), as in ἀφικνεῖσθαι, ἀφικνεῖσθαι, q.v.

ἀπολύω.g: I release, let go, send away, divorce
ἀπολύω.long: I release, let go, send away, divorce, am rid; mid: I depart.
ἀπολύω.sd: to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce
ἀπολύω.kj: (let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty
ἀπολύω.as:
ἀπο-λύω,
[in LXX for שׁוּב, etc., freq. in I-IV Mac;]
1.to set free, release: Lk 13:12, Jo 19:10, al.; a debtor, Mt 18:27; metaph., of forgiveness, Lk 6:37.
2.to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mt 15:23, Lk 2:299:12, Ac 19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mt 1:195:31, 3219:3, 8, 9, Mk 10:2, 4, 11, Lk 16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mk 10:12. Mid., to depart: Ac 28:25 (MM, s.v.).

ἀπαγγέλλω.g: I report, bring a report, announce
ἀπαγγέλλω.long: I report (from one place to another), bring a report, announce, declare.
ἀπαγγέλλω.kj: bring word (again), declare, report, shew (again), tell
ἀπαγγέλλω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
ἀπαγγέλλω.as:
ἀπ-αγγέλλω,
[in LXX chiefly for נגד hi.;]
of a messenger, speaker, or writer, to report, announce, declare: c. acc. rei, Ac 4:23, al.; c. dat. pers., Mt 2:8, al.; seq. ὅτι, Lk 18:37; πῶς, Lk 8:36; περί, Lk 7:1813:1, Ac 28:21, I Th 1:9; λέγων, Ac 22:26; c. acc. et inf., Ac 12:14; seq. εἰς, Mk 5:14, Lk 8:34 (MM, VGT, s.v.; Cremer, 25).

ἀπόλλυμι.long: (a) I kill, destroy, (b) I lose, mid: I am perishing (the resultant death being viewed as certain).
ἀπόλλυμι.sd: to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively
ἀπόλλυμι.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3639 (ὄλεθρος);
ἀπόλλυμι.as:
ἀπ-όλλυμι and ἀπολλύω,
[in LXX for אבד, etc. (38 words in all)].
1. Act.,
(1)to destroy utterly, destroy, kill: Mk 1:24, 9:22, al.; τ. ψνχήν, Mt 10:28, al.;
(2)to lose utterly: Mt 10:42, al.; metaph., of failing to save, Jo 6:3918:9.
2. Mid.,
(1)to perish;
(a) of things: Mt 5:29, Jo 6:12, He 1:11(LXX), al.;
(b) of persons: Mt 8:26, al. Metaph., of loss of eternal life, Jo 3:15, 1610:2817:12, Ro 2:12, I Co 8:1115:18, II Pe 3:9. In οἱ ἀπολλύμενοι, the perishing, contrasted in I Co 1:18, al., with οἱ σωζόμενοι, the "perfective" force of the verb, wh. "implies the completion of the process of destruction," is illustrated (v. M, Pr., 114 f.; M, Th., ii, 2:10);
(2)to be lost: Lk 15:421:18. Metaph., on the basis of the relation between shepherd and flock, of spiritual destitution and alienation from God: Mt 10:615:24, Lk 19:10 (MM, s.v.; DCG, i, 191 f., ii, 76, 554; Cremer, 451).

ἀποστέλλω.g: I send forth, send, send away, dismiss
ἀποστέλλω.long: I send forth, send (as a messenger, commission, etc.), send away, dismiss.
ἀποστέλλω.sd: set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively
ἀποστέλλω.kj: put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty)
ἀποστέλλω.as:
ἀπο-στέλλω,
[in LXX very freq., almost always for שׁלח;]
prop., to send away, to dispatch on service;
1.to send with a commission, or on service;
(a) of persons: Christ, Mt 10:40; the apostles, 10:16; servants, Mk 12:2; angels, 13:27;
(b) of things: ὄνος, Mt 21:3; τὸ δρέπανον, Mk 4:29; τ. λόγον, Ac 10:36; τ. ἐπαγγελίαν (i.e. the promised Holy Spirit), Lk 24:49, Rec.; seq. εἰς, Mt 20:2, Lk 11:49, Jo 3:17; ὀπίσω, Lk 19:14; ἔμπροσθεν, Jo 3:28; πρὸ προσώπου, Mt 11:10; πρός, Mt 21:34; with ref. to sender or place of departure: ἀπό, Lk 1:26 (Rec. ὑπό); παρά, Jo 1:6; ἐκ, Jo 1:19; ὑπό, Ac 10:17 (Rec. ἀπό); seq. inf., Mk 3:14, al.; ἵνα, Mk 12:2, al.; εἰς (of purpose), He 1:14; without direct obj.: seq. πρός, Jo 5:33; λέγων, Jo 11:3; ἀποστείλας, c. indic., Mt 2:16, Ac 7:14, Re 1:1.
2.to send away, dismiss: Lk 4:18, Mk 5:108:2612:3 (cf. ἐξ-, συν-αποστέλλω).
SYN.: πέμπω, the general term. ἀ. "suggests official or authoritative sending" (v. Thayer, s.v. πέμπω; Westc., Jo., 298; Epp. Jo., 125; Cremer, 529; MM, s.v.).

ἀπέρχομαι.g: I come or go away from, depart, return
ἀπέρχομαι.long: I come or go away from, depart, return, arrive, go after, follow.
ἀπέρχομαι.sd: to go off (i.e. depart), aside (i.e. apart) or behind (i.e. follow), literally or figuratively
ἀπέρχομαι.kj: come, depart, go (aside, away, back, out, … ways), pass away, be past
ἀπέρχομαι.as:
ἀπ-έρχομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for הלךְ;]
1.to go away, depart (also, in late writers, with "perfective" force, to arrive at a destination, the thought being carried on to the goal; M, Pr., 111 f., 247; MM, s.v.);
(a) absol.: Mt 13:25, al.; ptcp., ἀπελθών, used pleonastically with other verbs as in Heb. (Dalman, Words, 21), Mt 13:28, al.;
(b) with mention of place or person: εἰς, Mt 14:15; ἐπί, Lk 24:24; πρός, Re 10:9; ἀπό, Lk 1:38; ἐξω, Ac 4:15; ἐκεῖ, Mt 2:22.
2. As in LXX, seq. ὀπίσω, c. gen. (Heb. הָלַךְ אַחֲרֵי), to go after, follow: Mk 1:20, Jo 12:19; metaph., Mk 1:42, Re 21:1.

ἀποθήκη.as:
ἀπο-θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(< ἀποτίθημι), [in LXX for אוֹצָר, טֶנֶא, etc.;]
a storehouse, granary: Mt 3:126:2613:30, Lk 3:1712:18, 24.†

ἀποκρίνομαι.long: I answer, reply, take up the conversation.
ἀποκρίνομαι.sd: to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare H06030) to begin to speak (where an address is expected)
ἀποκρίνομαι.as:
ἀπο-κρίνω,
[in LXX chiefly for ענה;] in cl.,
1.to separate, distinguish.
2.to choose. Mid., to answer: Mt 27:12, Mk 14:61, Lk 3:1623:9, Jo 5:17, 19, Ac 3:12. In late Gk. the pass, also is used in this sense, and pass. forms are the more freq. in NT (M, Pr., 39, 161; MM, s.v.);
(a) in general sense: absol., Mk 12:34; c. acc. rei, Mt 22:46; c. dat. pers., Mt 12:38; seq. πρός, Ac 25:16;
(b) Hebraistically
(i) like ענה, to begin to speak, take up the conversation (Kennedy, Sources, 124 f.): Mt 11:25, al.,
(ii) redundant, as in the Heb. phrase וַיַּעַן וַיּאֹמֶר (Dalman, Words, 24 f., 38; M, Pr., 14; Bl., § 58, 4; 74, 2; Cremer, 374): ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπε, Mt 4:4; ἔφη, 8:8; λέγει, Mk 3:33; in Jo most freq. (ἀπεκ. κ. εἶπε, 1:49.

ἀποδίδωμι.long: (a) I give back, return, restore, (b) I give, render, as due, (c) mid: I sell.
ἀποδίδωμι.sd: to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications)
ἀποδίδωμι.kj: deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield
ἀποδίδωμι.as:
ἀπο-δίδωμι,
[in LXX for מכר, שׁוּב hi., נתן, שׁלם pi., etc.;]
to give up or back, restore, return: Mt 27:58, Lk 4:209:4219:8; esp. of wages, debts, oaths, etc. (MM, s.v.), to render what is due, to pay (Deiss., LAE, 334 f.): absol., Mt 18:25, 28, Lk 7:42. c. acc., Mt 5:2618:29, 30, 3420:821:4122:21, Mk 12:17, Lk 10:3512:5920:25, Ro 13:7, He 12:11, Re 22:2; ὅρκους, Mt 5:33 (cf. Nu 30:3, De 23:21 al.); of conjugal duty, τ. ὀφειλήν, I Co 7:3; ἀμοιβάς, I Ti 5:4; μαρτύριον, to give (as in duty bound) testimony, Ac 4:33; λόγον, to render account, Mt 12:36, Lk 16:2, Ac 19:40, He 13:17, I Pe 4:5; hence of requital, recompense, both in good and bad sense, Mt 6:4, 6, 1816:27, Ro 2:6, II Ti 4:8, 14, Re 18:622:12; κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ, Ro 12:17, I Th 5:15, I Pe 3:9. Mid., to give up of one's own, hence to sell (fr. Hdt. on): c. acc. rei, Ac 5:8, He 12:16; c. acc. pers., Ac 7:9 (cf. ἀντ-αποδίδωμι).†

ἀποστάσιον.long: repudiation, divorce; met: bill of divorce.
ἀποστάσιον.der: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868 (ἀφίστημι);
ἀποστάσιον.as:
ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό
(< ἀφίστημι), [in LXX; De 24:1, 3, Je 3:8, Is 50:1 (כְּרִיתֻת, כְּרִיתוּת)*;]
1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.).
2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mt 19:7, Mk 10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, s.v.), Mt 5:31 (for other late exx., v. MM, s.v.; Kennedy, Sources, 121).†

ἀποστρέφω.long: I turn away, pervert, remove; I restore, replace; mid: I desert, reject.
ἀποστρέφω.sd: to turn away or back (literally or figuratively)
ἀποστρέφω.as:
ἀπο-στρέφω,
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב;]
trans., c. acc.,
(a)to turn away, remove: Ro 11:26, II Ti 4:4; metaph., to turn away from allegiance, pervert: Lk 23:14;
(b)to turn back, return: μάχαιραν, Mt 26:52. Pass., reflex., to turn oneself away from: c. acc., Mt 5:42, II Ti 1:15, Tit 1:14, He 12:25; so act., absol., Ac 3:26 (cf. Si 8:5; Bl., § 53, 1; Cremer, 880).†

ἀπέχω.g: I have in full, am far, it is enough
ἀπέχω.long: I have in full, am far, it is enough.
ἀπέχω.sd: (actively) to have out, i.e. receive in full; (intransitively) to keep (oneself) away, i.e. be distant (literally or figuratively)
ἀπέχω.as:
ἀπ-έχω,
[in LXX chiefly for רחק;]
1. trans.,
(a)to hold back, keep off;
(b)to have in full, to have received (on the "punctiliar" force of the compound, v. M, Pr., 109, 247): c. acc., Mt 6:2, 5, 16, Lk 6:24, Phl 4:18, Phm 15 (for illustr. from π., where it is used in receipts, v. Deiss., BS, 229; LAE, 110 f.; MM, s.v.); impers., ἀπέχει (Field, Notes, 39), it is enough: Mk 14:41.
2. Intrans., to be away, distant: absol., Lk 15:20; seq. ἀπό, Mt 14:2415:8, Mk 7:6, Lk 7:615:2024:13. Mid., to abstain: c. gen., Ac 15:29, I Ti 4:3, I Pe 2:11; seq. ἀπό, Ac 15:20, I Th 4:35:22.†

ἁπλοῦς.sd: properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear)
ἁπλοῦς.der: probably from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and the base of G4120 (πλέκω);
ἁπλοῦς.as:
ἁπλοῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν
(contr. fr. -όος; < ἁ.- cop., πλόος), [in LXX: Pr 11:25*;]
simple, single: in a moral sense (DCG, ii, 628 f.), ἀφθαλμός, Mt 6:22, Lk 11:34. (In π. of a marriage dowry, v. MM, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἄδολος, ἄκακος, ἀκέραιος (Tr., Syn., § lvi; Cremer, 107, 639).

ἅπας.der: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and G3956 (πᾶς);
ἅπας.as:
ἅπας, -ασα, -αν
(strengthened form of πᾶς, v.s. ἅ-),
all, the whole, altogether: bef. subst. with art., as Lk 3:21; or after, as Mk 16:[15]; absol., in masc., as Lk 5:26; in neut., as Ac 2:44; ἅ. οὗτοι, Ac 2:7 (LT); ἅ. ὑμεῖς, Ga 3:28 (TTr.). Most freq. in Lk, Ac (v. MM, VG, s.v.).

ἀπάγω.long: I lead, carry, take away; met: I am led astray, seduced.
ἀπάγω.kj: bring, carry away, lead (away), put to death, take away
ἀπάγω.as:
ἀπ-άγω,
[in LXX for נהג, הלךְ hi., etc.;]
to lead away: Lk 13:15, Ac 23:1724:7 (R, mg.), I Co 12:2; esp. of leading to trial (so as law term in Attic), prison and death (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 26:5727:2, 31, Mk 14:44, 5315:16, Lk 21:1222:6623:26, Ac 12:19; of the direction of a way: Mt 7:13, 14 (cf. συν-απ-άγω).†

ἀπώλεια.long: destruction, ruin, loss, perishing; eternal ruin.
ἀπώλεια.sd: ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal)
ἀπώλεια.kj: damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste
ἀπώλεια.der: from a presumed derivative of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι);
ἀπώλεια.as:
ἀπώλεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀπόλλυμι), [in LXX (Cremer, 797) for אבד, אֵיד, etc.;]
destruction, waste, loss, perishing (in π., of money, v. MM, s.v.): Mt 26:8, Mk 14:4, Ac 8:20, Ro 9:22, I Ti 6:9, II Pe 2:1; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, perdition, the antithesis of σωτηρία: Mt 7:13, Jo 17:12, Phl 1:283:19, II Th 2:3, He 10:39, II Pe 2:33:7, 16, Re 17:8, 11 (DB, iii, 744).†

ἀποχωρέω.as:
ἀπο-χωρέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Je 26 (46):5 (סוּג), II Mac 4:33, III Mac 2:33*;]
to go away, depart, withdraw: seq. ἀπό, Mt 7:23, Lk 9:39, Ac 13:13 (absol., Lk 20:20, Tr., mg.).†

ἅπτω.sd: properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire
ἅπτω.as:
ἅπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for נגע;]
prop., to fasten to; hence, of fire, to kindle, light: Lk 8:1611:3315:8, Ac 28:2. Mid., c. gen., to fasten oneself to, cling to, lay hold of (so in π.; MM, s.v.): Mt 8:3, 15, Jo 20:17, al.; of carnal intercourse, I Co 7:1; with reference to levitical and ceremonial prohibitions, II Co 6:17, Col 2:21; of hostile action, I Jo 5:18 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-, περι-άπτω).
SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω. ἅ. is the stronger, θ., to touch, the lighter term. ψ. is to feel, as in search of something (Tr., Syn., § xvii; Lft., Col., 201 f.).

ἀποθνῄσκω.g: I am dying, am about to die
ἀποθνῄσκω.long: I am dying, am about to die, wither, decay.
ἀποθνῄσκω.kj: be dead, death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with)
ἀποθνῄσκω.as:
ἀπο-θνῄσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת;]
to die: of natural death, Mk 5:35, al.; of violent death (pass. of ἀποκτείνω), esp. of Christ, Mt 26:35, Jo 12:33, He 10:28, al.; of spiritual death, Jo 6:50, Ro 8:13, al.; c. dat. ref., Ro 6:2, 1014:7, 8, Ga 2:19; acc., ὅ, Ro 6:10; seq. ἐν, Mt 8:32, Jo 8:21, 24, I Co 15:22, He 11:37, Re 14:13; seq. ὑπέρ, περί, Jo 11:50, 5118:14, Ro 5:6-814:15, I Co 15:3, II Co 5:15, I Th 5:10, I Pe 3:18; ἀπό, Col 2:20; ἐκ, Re 8:11; fig., I Co 15:31 (cf. συν-αποθνήσκω, and V. Milligan, NTD, 258 f.; DCG, i, 791b; Cremer, 286; MM, s.v.; on the perfective force of this verb, M, Pr., 112, 114; and on the distinction bet. pres. and aor., M, Pr., 113 f.).

ἀπαίρω.long: I take away, remove; pass: I am taken away, withdrawn.
ἀπαίρω.as:
ἀπ-αίρω,
[in LXX chiefly for נסע;]
to lift off, hence, to take away; pass.: Mt 9:15, Mk 2:20, Lk 5:35.†

ἀπόστολος.g: an apostle, a messenger, an envoy, a delegate
ἀπόστολος.long: a messenger, envoy, delegate, one commissioned by another to represent him in some way, especially a man sent out by Jesus Christ Himself to preach the Gospel; an apostle.
ἀπόστολος.sd: a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers)
ἀπόστολος.kj: apostle, messenger, he that is sent
ἀπόστολος.as:
ἀπόστολος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἀποστέλλω), [in LXX; III Ki 14:6 A (שְׁלִיחַ)*;]
1.a fleet, an expedition (Dem.).
2.a messenger, one sent on a mission (Hdt., LXX, III Ki 14:6, and π.; v. M, Pr., 37 f.; MM, s.v.; M, Th., i, 2:7 and reff.): Jo 13:16, II Co 8:23, Phl 2:25.
3. In NT, an Apostle of Christ
(a) with special ref. to the Twelve: Mt 10:2, Mk 3:14, Lk 11:49, Eph 3:5, Re 18:20, al., equality with whom is claimed by St. Paul, Ga 1:1, 11 ff, I Ti 2:7, a1.;
(b) in a wider sense of prominent Christian teachers, as Barnabas, Ac 14:14, apparently also Silvanus and Timothy, I Th 2:6, and perhaps Andronicus and Junias (Junia?), Ro 16:7 (v. ICC, in l.); of false teachers, claiming apostleship: II Co 11:5, 13, Re 2:2. (On the different uses of the term in NT, v. Lft., Gal., 92-101; Cremer, 530; DB, i, 126; DCG, i, 105; Enc. Br., ii, 196 ff.)

ἀποκαλύπτω.g: I uncover, bring to light, reveal
ἀποκαλύπτω.long: I uncover, bring to light, reveal.
ἀποκαλύπτω.sd: to take off the cover, i.e. disclose
ἀποκαλύπτω.as:
ἀπο-καλύπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for גּלה;]
1. in general sense (cl.), to reveal, uncover, disclose,
(a) of things: Mt 10:26, Lk 2:3512:2, I Co 3:13;
(b) of persons: pass., Christ, Lk 17:30; Antichrist, II Th 2:3, 6, 8.
2. In LXX and NT, in special sense of divine revelation: Mt 11:25 (on the tense, v. M, Pr., 136), Mt 11:2716:17, Lk 10:21, 22, Jo 12:38, Ro 1:17, 188:18, I Co 2:1014:30, Ga 1:163:23, Eph 3:5, Phl 3:15, I Pe 1:5, 125:1 (Westc., Eph., 178 f.; M, Th., 149 f.).†
SYN.: φανερόω (v. Thayer, 62; Cremer, 342).†

ἀποκτείνω.long: I put to death, kill; fig: I abolish.
ἀποκτείνω.sd: to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy
ἀποκτείνω.as:
ἀπο-κτείνω
(also in late forms -κτέννω, Mt 10:28, a1., LTTr., -κτεννύω, Mk 12:5, WH), [in LXX for הרג, מוּת;]
to kill: Mt 14:5, al.; seq. instr. ἐν (q.v.), Eph 2:16, Re 2:23, al. Metaph.: Ro 7:11; τ. ἔχθραν, Eph 2:16; τὸ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει, II Co 3:6 (on the perfective force of this verb, v. M, Pr., 114).

ἀποκαθίστημι.long: I set up again, restore to its original position or condition; hence: I restore, give back.
ἀποκαθίστημι.sd: to reconstitute (in health, home or organization)
ἀποκαθίστημι.as:
ἀπο-καθ-ίστημι (ἀποκαθιστάω, Mk 9:12, Rec., -ιστάνω, LTTr.; cf. Ac 1:6; -κατιστάνω, WH),
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ;]
1.to restore, i.e. to a former condition: of health, Mt 12:13, Mk 3:58:25, Lk 6:10; of social or political affairs, Mt 17:11, Mk 9:12, Ac 1:6.
2.to give back, bring back: He 13:19 (so in π., MM, s.v.; cf. also Cremer, 312).†

ἀπάτη.as:
ἀπάτη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ec 9:6א (no Heb. equiv.), Jth 9:3, 10, 1316:8, IV Mac 18:8*;]
deceit, deceitfulness: Col 2:8; τοῦ πλούτου, Mt 13:22, Mk 4:19 (MM, VGT, s.v.); τῆς ἀδικίας, II Th 2:10; τῆς ἁμαρτίας, He 3:13; αἱ ἐπιθυμίαι τῆς ἀ., Eph 4:22. pl., ἀπάται (v. M, II Th. 2:10; NTD, 75; MM, VGT, s.v.): II Pe 2:13 (WH, mg., R., txt., ἐν ἀγάπαις).†

ἀπιστία.sd: faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience)
ἀπιστία.as:
** ἀπιστία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἄπιστος), [in LXX: Wi 14:25, IV Mac 12:4*;]
want of faith, unbelief: Mt 13:58, Mk 6:69:2416:14, Ro 3:3 (but v.s. ἀπιστέω) Ro 4:2011:20, 23, I Ti 1:13, He 3:12, 19 (DCG, ii, 775a; Cremer, 492).†

ἀποτίθημι.g: I lay off or aside, renounce
ἀποτίθημι.long: I lay off or aside, renounce, stow away, put.
ἀποτίθημι.kj: cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off)
ἀποτίθημι.as:
ἀπο-τίθημι,
[in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi.;]
to put off or aside; in NT always mid.,
(a)to put off from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Ac 7:58; metaph., in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Ro 13:12, Eph 4:22, 25, Col 3:8, He 12:1, Ja 1:21, I Pe 2:1;
(b)to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, s.v.), Mt 14:3.†

ἀποκεφαλίζω.as:
† ἀπο-κεφαλίζω
(< ἀπό, κεφαλή), [in LXX: Ps 151:7*;]
to behead: Mt 14:10, Mk 6:16, 28, Lk 9:9.†

ἀπαρνέομαι.long: I deny, disown, repudiate (either another person or myself), disregard.
ἀπαρνέομαι.sd: to deny utterly, i.e. disown, abstain
ἀπαρνέομαι.as:
ἀπ-αρνέομαι (-οῦμαι) depon.,
[in LXX: Is 31:7 (מאס)*;]
to deny, i.e. to refuse to recognize, to ignore: c. acc., of oneself (DCG, ii, 598 f.), Mt 16:24, Mk 8:34 (MM, VGT, s.v.), Lk 9:23 (WH, mg., txt., ἀρν-) of Peter's denials of Christ, Mt 26:34, 35, 75, Mk 14:30, 31, 72, Lk 22:34, 61; pass., Lk 12:9 (Cremer, 111).†

ἄπιστος.long: unbelieving, incredulous, unchristian; sometimes subst: unbeliever.
ἄπιστος.sd: (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing)
ἄπιστος.kj: that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing)
ἄπιστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4103 (πιστός);
ἄπιστος.as:
ἄ-πιστος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., πιστός), [in LXX: Pr 17:628:25, Is 17:10*;]
(a) of things, incredible: Ac 26:8;
(b) of persons, without faith or trust, unbelieving: Mt 17:17, Mk 9:19, Lk 9:4112:46, Jo 20:27, Tit 1:15, Re 21:8; specif., of unbelievers as opp. to Christians: I Co 6:67:12-1510:2714:22-24, II Co 4:46:14, 15, I Ti 5:8 (cf. Lft., Notes, 265; Cremer, 491).†

ἀποδημέω.long: I am away from home, go into another country, am away, am abroad.
ἀποδημέω.sd: to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land
ἀποδημέω.kj: go (travel) into a far country, journey
ἀποδημέω.as:
ἀπο-δημέω, -ῶ
(< ἀπόδημος), [in LXX: Ez 19:3 A*;]
to be or go abroad (M, Pr., 1302): Mt 21:3325:14, 15, Mk 12:1, Lk 15:1320:9.†

ἀποδοκιμάζω.g: I reject after testing, I disqualify
ἀποδοκιμάζω.sd: to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate
ἀποδοκιμάζω.as:
ἀπο-δοκιμάζω,
[in LXX: Ps 117 (118):22, al. (מאס);]
to reject: Mt 21:42(LXX), Mk 8:3112:10(LXX), Lk 9:2217:2520:17(LXX), He 12:17, I Pe 2:4, 7(LXX) (Cremer, 701; MM, s.v.).†

ἀποδεκατόω.g: I take off a tenth part, pay tithe
ἀποδεκατόω.long: I take off (deduct) a tenth part (of my property) (and give it away), pay tithe.
ἀποδεκατόω.as:
† ἀπο-δεκατόω,
[in LXX for עשׂר in both senses foll., e.g. (1) Ge 28:22 (2) I Ki 8:15;]
1. c. acc. rei, to tithe, pay a tenth of: Mt 23:23, Lk 11:42.
2. C. acc. pers., to exact tithes from: He 7:5.
3.to decimate (Socr., HE, 573 A; v. Kennedy, Sources, 117).†

ἁπαλός.long: soft, tender, as a shoot of a tree.
ἁπαλός.as:
ἀπαλός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX for רַךְ;]
tender: Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28.†

ἀπάντησις.g: the act of meeting, to meet
ἀπάντησις.long: the act of meeting, to meet (a phrase seemingly almost technical for the reception of a newly arrived official).
ἀπάντησις.as:
ἀπάντησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀπαντάω), [in LXX chiefly for לִקְרַאת;]
usually with v.l., ὑπ-; a meeting; εἰς ἀ., c. gen. or dat., to meet: Mt 25:627:32 (WH, txt., omits), Ac 28:15, I Th 4:17 (v. M, Th., in l.; M, Pr., 14, 242; MM, VGT, s.v.; Lft., Notes, 69).†

ἀποσπάω.g: I wrench away from, drag away, withdraw
ἀποσπάω.long: lit: I wrench away from, drag away, but perhaps sometimes in the well-attested weakened sense: I am parted or withdrawn.
ἀποσπάω.sd: to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously)
ἀποσπάω.as:
ἀπο-σπάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for נתק: ni., hi., etc.;]
to draw off or away, tear away (MM, s.v.): Ac 20:30; μάχαιραν, draw a sword, Mt 26:51; pass., to be parted or withdrawn (Field, Notes, 134; but v. Thayer, s.v.), Lk 22:41, Ac 21:1.†

ἀπάγχομαι.long: I choke, strangle; mid: I strangle or hang myself.
ἀπάγχομαι.sd: akin to the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); to strangle oneself off (i.e. to death)
ἀπάγχομαι.as:
ἀπ-άγχω
(< ἄγχω, to press, strangle), [in LXX: II Ki 17:23 (חנק), To 3:10*;]
to strangle; mid., to hang oneself (or, to choke; v. M, Pr., 155): Mt 27:5.†

ἀπονίπτω.sd: to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically)
ἀπονίπτω.as:
ἀπο-νίπτω,
[in LXX for שׁטף, רחץ, מחה;]
to wash off: mid. (reflex.), τ. χεῖρας, Mt 27:24.†

ἀπέναντι.g: over against, opposite, in view of, in the presence of
ἀπέναντι.long: against, over against, opposite, in view of, in the presence of.
ἀπέναντι.sd: from in front, i.e. opposite, before or against
ἀπέναντι.kj: before, contrary, over against, in the presence of
ἀπέναντι.as:
† ἀπ-έναντι,
adv. c. gen. (Hellenistic, common in LXX);
1.over against (MM, s.v.): Mt 27:61, Mk 12:41, WH, mg.
2.before, in the presence of: Mt 27:24 (WH, mg.), Ac 3:16, Ro 3:18.
3.against: Ac 17:7.†

ἀποκυλίω.as:
† ἀπο-κυλίω
(v.s. κυλίω), [in LXX: Ge 29:3, 8, 10 (גּלל) Jth 13:9*;]
to roll away: Mt 28:2, Mk 16:3, Lk 24:2.†

ἀποστεγάζω.g: I unroof, take the roof off
ἀποστεγάζω.long: I unroof, take the roof off.
ἀποστεγάζω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4721 (στέγη);
ἀποστεγάζω.as:
** ἀπο-στεγάζω
(< στέγη), [in Sm.: Je 49:10 (29:11)*;]
to unroof: Mk 2:4.†

ἀπόκρυφος.as:
ἀπόκρυφος, -ον
(< ἀποκρύπτω), [in LXX Chiefly for סֵתֶר;]
hidden: Mk 4:22, Lk 8:17, Col 2:3 (v. Lft., in l.; MM, s.v.).†

ἀπορέω.g: I am in difficulties, am at my wits end
ἀπορέω.long: I am at a loss, am perplexed; mid: I am in doubt.
ἀπορέω.sd: to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally)
ἀπορέω.der: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4198 (πορεύομαι);
ἀπορέω.as:
ἀπορέω, -ῶ
(< ἄπορος, ἀ- neg., πόρος, a way, resource), [in LXX for צרר, מוּךְ, etc.;]
to be at a loss, be perplexed: absol., Mk 6:20 (ἐποίει, R, mg.); mid., be in doubt: absol., II Co 4:8; c. acc., Ac 25:20; seq. περί, Lk 24:4; ἐν, Ga 4:20; περὶ τίνος λέγει, Jo 13:22.†
SYN.: διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, διστάζω, μετεωρίζομαι (v. DCG, i, 491).

ἀποτάσσομαι.g: I withdraw from, take leave of, renounce, send away
ἀποτάσσομαι.long: I withdraw from, take leave of, renounce, send away.
ἀποτάσσομαι.sd: literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce
ἀποτάσσομαι.kj: bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away
ἀποτάσσομαι.der: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G5021 (τάσσω);
ἀποτάσσομαι.as:
ἀπο-τάσσω,
[in LXX: Ec 2:20 (יאשׁ pi.), I Es 6:27, Je 20:2, I Mac4*;]
to set apart. Mid., in late Gk. (Bl., § 37, 1; Swete, Mk., 136 f.; MM, s.v.), c. dat.,
(a)to take leave of: Mk 6:46, Lk 9:61, Ac 18:18, 21, II Co 2:13;
(b)to forsake: Lk 14:33.†

ἀπολαμβάνω.long: (a) I get back, receive back, (b) I get (receive) as due (deserved), (c) mid: I draw aside, separate.
ἀπολαμβάνω.sd: to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside
ἀπολαμβάνω.as:
ἀπο-λαμβάνω,
[in LXX: Nu 34:14 (לקח (De 25:5 A, Is 5:17, II Mac 4:466:218:6, IV Mac 18:23*;]
1.to receive from another; absol., to receive as one's due: Lk 16:2518:30 (v.l. λάβῃ) 23:41, Ro 1:27, Ga 4:5, Col 3:24, II Jo 8.
2.to receive back: Lk 6:3415:27.
3.to take apart or aside: Mk 7:33 (cf. use in π. of the recluses of the Serapeum; MM, s.v.).†

ἀποκόπτω.long: I smite, cut off, cut loose; mid: I emasculate, castrate, mutilate myself.
ἀποκόπτω.sd: to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts)
ἀποκόπτω.as:
ἀπο-κόπτω,
[in LXX for קצץ, כּרת, etc.;]
to cut off: Mk 9:43, 45, Jo 18:10, 26, Ac 27:32. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated: Ga 5:12 (cf. De 23:1 LXX; and v. Cremer, 751; MM, s.v.).†

ἀποστερέω.g: I deprive one of something, rob
ἀποστερέω.long: I defraud, deprive of, despoil; mid: I endure deprivation; pass: I am bereft of.
ἀποστερέω.kj: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud
ἀποστερέω.as:
ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ
(< στερέω, to rob), [in LXX: Ex 21:10 (גּרע), De 24:14 (עשׁק), Ma 3:5, Si 4:129:6, 731 (34):21, 22*;]
to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, s.v.): absol., Mk 10:19, I Co 6:8; c. acc. pers., I Co 7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: I Co 6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but v. Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: I Ti 6:5.†

ἀποβάλλω.g: I throw away from, throw overboard
ἀποβάλλω.long: I throw away from, throw overboard, cast aside.
ἀποβάλλω.sd: to throw off; figuratively, to lose
ἀποβάλλω.as:
ἀπο-βάλλω,
[in LXX: Is 1:30 (נבל) and elsew. without Heb. equiv.;]
to throw off: Mk 10:50; metaph., to lose, let go (Field, Notes, 231 f.; MM, s.v.): He 10:35.†

ἀποπλανάω.g: I cause to wander astray, have wandered away
ἀποπλανάω.long: I cause to go astray; pass: I am led astray.
ἀποπλανάω.sd: to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth)
ἀποπλανάω.as:
ἀπο-πλανάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for נדח hi., נטה hi., שׁוּב pi.;]
to cause to go astray; metaph., of leading into error: Mk 13:22; pass., to be led astray: I Ti 6:10.†

ἀπόδημος.long: away from home, sojourning in another country.
ἀπόδημος.sd: absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller
ἀπόδημος.as:
* ἀπό-δημος, -ον,
gone abroad (RV, sojourning in another country): Mk 13:34.†

ἀπαντάω.long: I go to meet, meet, encounter.
ἀπαντάω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί);
ἀπαντάω.as:
ἀπαντάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for פּגע;]
1.to go to meet.
2.to meet; c. dat.: Mk 14:13, Lk 17:12 (WH, mg., ὑπ-; in Rec. freq. as v.1. for ὑπ-, q.v.).†

ἀποφέρω.long: I carry, bear away (sometimes with violence).
ἀποφέρω.as:
ἀπο-φέρω,
[in LXX for הלךְ, etc.;]
to carry off, bear, or lead away: c. acc., Mk 15:1, I Co 16:3, Re 17:321:10. Pass., Lk 16:22, Ac 19:12.†

ἀπιστέω.long: I am unfaithful, disbelieve, refuse belief, prove false.
ἀπιστέω.sd: to be unbelieving, i.e. (transitively) disbelieve, or (by implication) disobey
ἀπιστέω.as:
** ἀπιστέω, -ῶ
(< ἄπιστος), [in LXX: Wi 1:210:712:1718:13, Si 1:27, II Mac 8:13*;]
1.to disbelieve, be faithless: Mk 16:11, 16, Lk 24:11, 41, Ac 28:24, I Pe 2:7; so prob. also Ro 3:3, II Ti 2:13 (ICC, CGT, in ll.; MM, s.v.).
2. = ἀπειθέω (Hdt.; on this sense in Ro 3:3, II Ti 2:13, v. Vaughan on Ro 3:3; Lft., Notes, 265; Thayer, s.v.).†

ἀπειθής.long: unbelieving, disobedient, who will not be persuaded.
ἀπειθής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3982 (πείθω);
ἀπειθής.as:
ἀπειθής, -ές
(< πείθομαι), [in LXX for מרה, מְרִי, סרר;]
disobedient: absol., Lk 1:17, Tit 1:163:3; c. dat., Ac 26:19, Ro 1:30, II Ti 3:2.†

ἀπογράφω.g: I enroll, inscribe in a register
ἀπογράφω.long: I enroll, inscribe in a register; mid: I give my name for registration (or census-taking).
ἀπογράφω.sd: to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol
ἀπογράφω.as:
ἀπο-γράφω,
[in LXX: Jg 8:14, Pr 22:20 (כּתב), I Es 8:30, III Mac 2:294:146:34, 38*;]
1.to write out, copy.
2.to enrol; mid., to enrol oneself: Lk 2:1 (M, Pr., 162; but. v. ICC, in l.), Lk 2:3, 5; pass., He 12:23 (v. reff., s.v. ἀπογραφή).†

ἀπογραφή.sd: an enrollment; by implication, an assessment
ἀπογραφή.as:
ἀπο-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀπογράφω),
[in LXX: Da LXX 10:21 (כְּתָב), I Es 8:30, AB, II Mac 2:1, III Mac 2:324:15, 177:22*;]
1.a written copy.
2. As law term, a deposition (Demos.).
3. In late writers, a register, enrolment, census (MM, s.v.; Deiss., LAE, 160, 268 f.): Lk 2:2, Ac 5:37.†

ἀποκάλυψις.kj: appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation
ἀποκάλυψις.as:
ἀπο-κάλυψις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποκαλύπτω), [in LXX: I Ki 20:30 (עֶרְוָה), Si 11:2722:2242:1*;]
an uncovering, laying bare (Plut.). Metaph., a revealing, revelation: a disclosure of divine truth, or a manifestion from God: Lk 2:32, Ro 2:58:1916:25, I Co 1:714:6, 26, II Co 12:1, 7, Ga 1:122:2, Eph 1:173:3, II Th 1:7, I Pe 1:7, 134:13, Re 1:1.†
SYN.: ἐπιφάνεια, παρουσία, φανέρωσις (v. Tr., Syn., xciv; Lft., Notes, 102, 178; Westc, Eph., 178 f.; M, Th., 145 ff.; Cremer, 343).

ἀπόκρισις.as:
ἀπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποκρίνομαι), [in LXX for דּבר, etc.;]
an answering, an answer: Lk 2:4720:26, Jo 1:2219:9.†

ἀποβαίνω.g: I go or come out of, disembark, result
ἀποβαίνω.long: I go or come out of, disembark, turn out, result, become, happen.
ἀποβαίνω.sd: literally, to disembark; figuratively, to eventuate
ἀποβαίνω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
ἀποβαίνω.as:
ἀπο-βαίνω,
[in LXX for היה, etc.;]
to step off, disembark: Lk 5:2, Jo 21:9; metaph., of events, to issue, turn out (Field, Notes, 74): Lk 21:13, Phl 1:19 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπαιτέω.g: I ask back, ask what is my due
ἀπαιτέω.long: I ask back, ask what is my due, demand back.
ἀπαιτέω.as:
ἀπ-αιτέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: De 15:2, 3, al. (נגשׂ), Si 20:15, Wi 15:8, al.;]
to ask back, demand back: Lk 6:3012:20 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀπελπίζω.long: I give up in despair, despair of; I hope to receive from or in return.
ἀπελπίζω.sd: to hope out, i.e. fully expect
ἀπελπίζω.as:
† ἀπ-ελπίζω,
[in LXX: Is 29:19 (אֶבְיוֹן), Jth 9:11, Es 4:17, Si 22:2127:21, II Mac 9:18*;]
1.to give up in despair, despair of (Polyb., Diod., LXX).
2.to hope to receive from or in return (Field, Notes, 59; Cremer, 712; Soph., Lex., s.v.): c. acc. (M; Pr., 65; MM, s.v.), Lk 6:35.†

ἀποπνίγω.g: I suffocate, choke, drown, stop the growth of
ἀποπνίγω.long: (a) I suffocate, choke, drown, (b) I stop the growth of.
ἀποπνίγω.as:
ἀπο-πνίγω,
[in LXX: Na 2:12 (13) (חנק pi.), To 3:8*;]
to choke: Mt 13:7, Lk 8:7; pass., of drowning (= καταποντίζομαι), Lk 8:33.†

ἀποδέχομαι.long: I receive, welcome, entertain (with hospitality), embrace.
ἀποδέχομαι.sd: to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve (things)
ἀποδέχομαι.as:
** ἀπο-δέχομαι
[in LXX: To 7:17, Jth 13:13; Jdt.13.1, I-IV Mac10*;]
to accept gladly, welcome, receive: Lk 8:409:11, Ac 18:2721:1728:30; metaph., c. acc. rei, Ac 2:4124:3 (MM, s.v.; Cremer, 688).†

ἀποθλίβω.long: (lit: I rub), jostle, press hard, crowd.
ἀποθλίβω.as:
ἀπο-θλίβω,
[in LXX for לחץ, Nu 22:25*;]
to press hard: Lk 8:45.†

ἀποτινάσσω.as:
ἀπο-τινάσσω,
[in LXX: Jg 16:20 A (נער ni.), I Ki 10:2 (נטשׁ), La 2:7 (נאר pi.)*;]
to shake of: Lk 9:5, Ac 28:5.†

ἀπομάσσομαι.long: I wipe off, wipe clean; mid: I wipe myself off.
ἀπομάσσομαι.der: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and (to squeeze, knead, smear);
ἀπομάσσομαι.as:
** ἀπο-μάσσω
(< μάσσω, Att. -ττω, to touch, handle), [in LXX: To 7:17*;]
to wipe off, wipe clean: mid., Lk 10:11.†

ἀποκρύπτω.long: I hide away, conceal, keep secret.
ἀποκρύπτω.sd: to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep secret
ἀποκρύπτω.as:
ἀπο-κρύπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for סתר;]
to hide, conceal, keep secret: c. acc., Lk 10:21; pass., I Co 2:7, Eph 3:9, Col 1:26 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀποστοματίζω.sd: to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner)
ἀποστοματίζω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a (presumed) derivative of G4750 (στόμα);
ἀποστοματίζω.as:
* ἀποστοματίζω
(< στόμα),
1. In cl., to speak from memory, to dictate to a pupil (Plat.).
2. In late Gk., to catechize, question: Lk 11:53 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπολογέομαι.g: I give a defense, defend myself
ἀπολογέομαι.long: I give a defense, defend myself (especially in a law court): it can take an object of what is said in defense.
ἀπολογέομαι.sd: to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self)
ἀπολογέομαι.kj: answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self
ἀπολογέομαι.der: middle voice from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3056 (λόγος);
ἀπολογέομαι.as:
ἀπολογέομαι, -οῦμαι
(< ἀπό, λόγος), [in LXX: Je 12:1 (ויבperhaps a misspelling of ריב #7378) 38 (31):6, II Mac 13:26*;]
1.to defend: c. acc., Ro 2:15.
2.to defend one's self: absol., Lk 21:14, Ac 26:1; seq. ὅτι, Ac 25:8; τί, to adduce something in one's defence, Lk 12:11, Ac 26:24 (ταῦτα) 24:10 (τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ); περί, c. gen. rei, and ἐπί, c. gen. pers., Ac 26:2; c. dat. pers., Ac 19:33, II Co 12:19.†

ἀπαλλάσσω.long: I free (a person) from (anything), oftener in the middle voice: I am released from, am rid of (a person or thing), depart.
ἀπαλλάσσω.sd: to change away, i.e. release, (reflexively) remove
ἀπαλλάσσω.as:
ἀπ-αλλάσσω,
[in LXX for סוּר hi., etc.;]
to remove, release: He 2:15; pass., to depart: Ac 19:12; in legal sense (MM, VGT, s.v.), seq. ἀπό, c. gen. pers., to be quit of: Lk 12:58 (Cremer, 90, 632).†

ἀποκλείω.long: I shut fast, close, shut up.
ἀποκλείω.as:
ἀπο-κλείω,
[in LXX chiefly for סגר;]
to shut fast: Lk 13:25.†

ἀποτελέω.g: I complete, accomplish, form fully, perfect
ἀποτελέω.long: I complete, accomplish, form fully, perfect, bring to maturity.
ἀποτελέω.as:
** ἀπο-τελέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: I Es 5:73, I Mac 15:39*;]
to bring to an end, complete, accomplish (cf. MM, s.v.): Lk 13:32, Ja 1:15.†

ἀπαρτισμός.as:
*† ἀπαρτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἀπαρτίζω, to finish),
completion: Lk 14:28 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀπόκειμαι.g: I have been put away, am stored, am reserved for
ἀπόκειμαι.long: I have been put away, am stored, am reserved for.
ἀπόκειμαι.sd: to be reserved; figuratively, to await
ἀπόκειμαι.as:
ἀπό-κειμαι,
[in LXX: Ge 49:10 (שִׁילֹה), Jb 38:23 (חשׂךְ), II Mac 12:45, IV Mac 8:11*;]
to be laid up, in store, laid away: Lk 19:20. Metaph., c. dat. pers., to be reserved (Dem., Plat.; and v. MM, s.v.): Col 1:5, II Ti 4:8, He 9:27.†

ἀπορία.as:
ἀπορία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀπορέω), [in LXX for בֶּהָלָה, etc.;]
perplexity: Lk 21:25 (MM, s.v.; on the construction, v. Field, Notes, 74 f.).†

ἀποψύχω.g: I faint, breathe out life, die
ἀποψύχω.long: I faint, breathe out life, die, am dismayed.
ἀποψύχω.as:
** ἀπο-ψύχω,
[in LXX: IV Mac 15:18*;]
1.to breathe out life, expire (Thuc.; LXX, IV Mac 15:18).
2.to leave off breathing, faint (Hom., Od., xxiv, 348): seq. ἀπό, Lk 21:26.†

ἀπολύτρωσις.long: release effected by payment of ransom; redemption, deliverance.
ἀπολύτρωσις.sd: (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation
ἀπολύτρωσις.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3083 (λύτρον);
ἀπολύτρωσις.as:
† ἀπο-λύτρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀπολυτρόω, to release on payment of ransom, cf. λύτρον), [in LXX: Da (LXX) 4:30c*;]
release effected by payment of ransom, redemption, deliverance; metaph., He 11:35; of deliverance thr. Christ from evil and the consequences of sin: Lk 21:28, Ro 3:24 (Vau., in l.) 8:23, I Co 1:30, Eph 1:7, 144:30, Col 1:14, He 9:15. (On the extent to wh. the word retains the sense of ransom, v. ICC, Ro., 3:24, Westc., He., 297 ff.; v. also ICC, Eph., 11; DCG, ii, 605; Cremer, 410; Deiss., LAE, 331; Lft., Notes, 271, 316; Tr., Syn., § lxxvii.)†

ἀπειθέω.long: I disobey, rebel, am disloyal, refuse conformity.
ἀπειθέω.kj: not believe, disobedient, obey not, unbelieving
ἀπειθέω.as:
ἀπειθέω, -ῶ
(< ἀπειθής), [in LXX for מרה, סרר, etc.;]
as in cl. (MM, VGT, s.v.); to disobey, be disobedient: absol., Ac 14:219:9, Ro 10:2111:3115:31, He 3:1811:31, I Pe 3:20; c. dat., Jo 3:36, Ro 2:811:30, I Pe 2:83:14:17 (Cremer, 475).†

ἀποσυνάγωγος.long: away from the synagogue, expelled from the synagogue, excommunicated.
ἀποσυνάγωγος.as:
*† ἀποσυνάγωγος, -ον
(< συναγωγή),
expelled from the congregation (Field, Notes, 96), excommunicated: Jo 9:2212:4216:2 (Cremer, 64, 607).†

ἀποστολή.as:
ἀπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀποστέλλω), [in LXX: De 22:7, III Ki 4:349:16, Ps 77 (78):49, Ec 8:8, Ca 4:13 (for שׁלח and its cognates), I Es 9:51, 54, Je 39 (32):36, Ba 2:25, I Mac 2:18, II Mac 3:2*.]
1. In cl., a sending away (MM, s.v.), as, an expedition (Hdt.).
2. In LXX
(a)discharge, dismissal (Ec 8:8);
(b)a gift (III Ki 9:16, I Mac 2:13).
3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: Ac 1:25, Ro 1:5, I Co 9:2, Ga 2:8 (Cremer, 530).†

ἀποφθέγγομαι.as:
† ἀπο-φθέγγομαι,
[in LXX for נבא, etc.;]
to speak forth, give utterance: Ac 2:4, 1426:25 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀποδείκνυμι.g: I show by proof, demonstrate, set forth
ἀποδείκνυμι.long: I show by proof, demonstrate, set forth, proclaim to an officer.
ἀποδείκνυμι.sd: to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit
ἀποδείκνυμι.as:
ἀπο-δείκνυμι,
[in LXX: Es 2:9 (ראה), al.;]
1.to bring out, show forth, exhibit (Lft., Notes, 200; ICC, in l.): I Co 4:9.
2.to declare, show: Ac 2:22.
3.to prove: Ac 25:7.
4. As freq. in late Gk., to proclaim to an office: seq. ὅτι, II Th 2:4 (Milligan, in l.; MM, s.v.; Lft., Notes. 113.)†

ἀποκατάστασις.as:
* ἀπο-κατά-στασις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποκαθίστημι),
restoration: Ac 3:21 (in π. of repairs and restorations of temples, v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀπειλέω.sd: to menace; by implication, to forbid
ἀπειλέω.as:
ἀπειλέω, -ῶ
(ἀπειλή), [in LXX: Na 1:4 (גּער), Is 66:14 (זעם), Si 19:17, al.;]
to threaten: I Pe 2:23; mid., Ac 4:17 (v. MM, VGT, s.v., and cf. προσαπειλέω).†

ἀπειλή.as:
ἀπειλή, -ῆ, ἡ,
[in LXX for גְּעָרָה, etc.;]
threatening, threat: Ac 4:299:1, Eph 6:9.†

ἀπωθέομαι.g: I push or thrust away, reject
ἀπωθέομαι.long: I push (thrust) away, repulse, reject, refuse.
ἀπωθέομαι.sd: to push off, figuratively, to reject
ἀπωθέομαι.kj: cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from)
ἀπωθέομαι.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of or (to shove);
ἀπωθέομαι.as:
ἀπ-ωθέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for זנח, מאס, etc.;]
to thrust away. Mid., to thrust away from oneself, refuse, reject: c. acc. pers. (MM, s.v.), Ac 7:27, 3913:46, Ro 11:1, 2, I Ti 1:19.†

ἀπερίτμητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4059 (περιτέμνω);
ἀπερίτμητος.as:
† ἀ-περί-τμητος, -ον
(< περιτέμνω), [in LXX chiefly for עָרֵל;]
uncircumcised; metaph. (τ.) καρδίαις (cf. Je 9:26, al.): Ac 7:51. (ἄσημος, found in π., appears to have been the word used by Greek-speaking Egyptians: v. Deiss., BS, 153; cf. also Cremer, 885; MM, s.v.)†

ἀποπίπτω.g: I fall away from, fall off
ἀποπίπτω.as:
ἀπο-πίπτω,
[in LXX for מלל, נפל, etc.;]
to fall off: Ac 9:18.†

ἀποπλέω.as:
* ἀπο-πλέω, -ῶ,
to sail away: Ac 13:414:2620:1527:1 (Burton, 159).†

ἀποχωρίζομαι.long: I separate from; mid: I part; pass: I am swept aside.
ἀποχωρίζομαι.sd: to rend apart; reflexively, to separate
ἀποχωρίζομαι.as:
ἀπο-χωρίζω,
[in LXX: Ez 43:21 (מִפְקָד)*;]
to separate, part asunder: pass., Re 6:14; reflexively, to separate oneself: Ac 15:39.†

Ἀπολλωνία.sd: from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia
Ἀπολλωνία.der: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun;
Ἀπολλωνία.as:
Ἀπολλωνία, -ας, ἡ,
Apollonia, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:1.†

ἄπειμι.as:
ἄπ-ειμι
(εἰμί, sum), [in LXX for כּחד ni., נדח ni.;]
to be absent: I Co 5:3, II Co 10:1, 1113:2, 10, Phl 1:27, Col 2:5.†

ἀπελαύνω.as:
ἀπ-ελαύνω,
[in LXX for נצל, שׁלח;]
to drive away: Ac 18:16 (MM, s.v.).†

Ἀπολλῶς.der: probably from the same as G624 (Ἀπολλωνία);
Ἀπολλῶς.as:
Ἀπολλώς, -ώ, ὁ
(perh. contr. from Ἀπολλώνιος, Ac 18:24 D),
Apollos: Ac 18:2419:1, I Co 1:123:4-6, 224:616:12, Tit 3:13.†

ἀπελεγμός.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω);
ἀπελεγμός.as:
*† ἀπ-ελεγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἀπελέγχω, to convict, refute),
refutation, disrepute: ἐλθεῖν εἰς ἀ., Ac 19:27 (not elsewhere; v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀποφορτίζομαι.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of G5412 (φορτίζω);
ἀποφορτίζομαι.as:
*† ἀπο-φορτίζομαι
(< φορτίζω, to load),
to discharge a cargo (Field, Notes, 134), to unlade: c. acc., τ. γόμον, Ac 21:3.†

ἀποστασία.der: feminine of the same as G647 (ἀποστάσιον);
ἀποστασία.as:
† ἀποστασία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀφίστημι), [in LXX for מַעַל, etc.;]
defection, apostasy, revolt; in late Gk. (MM, Exp., viii; Lft., Notes, 111; Cremer, 308) for cl. ἀπόστασις, freq. in sense of political revolt, in LXX (e.g. Jos 22:22, II Ch 29:19, Je 2:19) and NT always of religious apostasy: Ac 21:21, II Th 2:3.†

ἀπολογία.long: a verbal defense (particularly in a law court).
ἀπολογία.kj: answer (for self), clearing of self, defence
ἀπολογία.as:
** ἀπολογία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀπολογέομαι), [in LXX: Wi 6:10*;]
a speech in defence: Ac 25:16, II Co 7:11, Phl 1:7, 16, II Ti 4:16; c. dat. pers., I Co 9:3, I Pe 3:15; seq. πρός, Ac 22:1.†

ἀπολούομαι.long: I wash off, mid: I wash away (my sins, in baptism).
ἀπολούομαι.sd: to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively)
ἀπολούομαι.as:
ἀπο-λούω,
[in LXX: Jb 9:30 (רחץ)*;]
to wash off, wash away; mid., metaph., c. acc. rei, to wash off oneself: ἁμαρτίας, Ac 22:16; absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean (cf. Cremer, 406), I Co 6:11.†

ἀπρόσκοπος.g: not offending, not causing offence, blameless
ἀπρόσκοπος.long: (free from hurt or harm, hence) not offending, not causing offence, blameless.
ἀπρόσκοπος.sd: actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin
ἀπρόσκοπος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4350 (προσκόπτω);
ἀπρόσκοπος.as:
**† ἀπρόσκοπος, -ον
(< προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Si 35 (32):21, III Mac 3:8*;]
1. act., not causing to stumble: metaph., of not leading others into sin, I Co 10:32.
2. Pass., not stumbling, without offence, blameless: Ac 24:16, Phl 1:10 (for exx., v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀποβολή.long: a casting away, rejection, a loss.
ἀποβολή.as:
* ἀπο-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀποβάλλω);
1.a throwing away, rejection: opp. to πρόσλημψις, Ro 11:15.
2.a losing, loss: Ac 27:22.†

ἀπορίπτω.g: I throw away from, throw overboard
ἀπορίπτω.long: I throw away from, throw overboard.
ἀπορίπτω.as:
ἀπο-ρίπτω (Rec. -ρρίπτω, c1.),
[in LXX for שׁלךְ hi., etc.;]
to throw away, cast forth: reflexively, Ac 27:43 (EV, cast themselves overboard; v. MM, s.v.).†

Ἀππίου.long: the township Appi Forum on the Appian Way, 43 Roman miles from Rome, was named.
Ἀππίου.sd: (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman
Ἀππίου.as:
Ἄππιος, -ου, ὁ,
Appius; Ἀππίου Φόρον, Appii Forum (Market of Appius), a town in Italy: Ac 28:15.†

ἀποκαραδοκία.der: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of (the head) and G1380 (δοκέω) (in the sense of watching);
ἀποκαραδοκία.as:
*† ἀπο-καραδοκία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀποκαραδοκέω, used by Aq. in Ps 36 (37):7 for התהוֹלל; < ἀπό, κάραthe head, δοκέω, in Ion., to watch),
to watch with outstretched head, watch anxiously (Polyb., π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 3745, 377 f.), Ro 8:19, Phl 1:20 (Lft., in l.; Cremer, 177).†

ἀπεκδέχομαι.g: I expect eagerly, wait for eagerly
ἀπεκδέχομαι.long: I expect eagerly, wait for eagerly, look for.
ἀπεκδέχομαι.as:
*† ἀπ-εκ-δέχομαι, depon.,
to await or expect eagerly (Lft., Notes, 149; MM, VGT, s.v.): absol., I Pe 3:20; c. acc. rei, Ro 8:19, 23, 25, I Co 1:7, Ga 5:5; c. acc. pers., Phl 3:20, He 9:28.†

ἀπαρχή.long: the first-fruits, the earliest crop of the year, hence also met., for example, of the earliest converts in a district; there is evidence in favor of rendering in some passages merely by: sacrifice, gift.
ἀπαρχή.sd: a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively)
ἀπαρχή.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G756 (ἄρχομαι);
ἀπαρχή.as:
ἀπ-αρχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀπάρχομαι, to make a beginning in sacrifice, offer first fruits), [in LXX chiefly for תְּרוּמָה, רֵאשִׁית;]
1.the beginning of a sacrifice.
2.first fruits: τοῦ φυράματος (cf. Nu 15:20), Ro 11:16. Metaph., ἀ. τοῦ πνεύματος: Ro 8:23; of Christians: Ro 16:5, I Co 16:15, II Th 2:13 (WH, mg., R, mg., txt., ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς; v. Lft., Notes, 119 f.), Ja 1:18, Re 14:4; of Christ: I Co 15:20, 23 (Cremer, 117; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀποτολμάω.as:
* ἀπο-τολμάω, -ῶ,
to be quite bold, make a bold venture: Ro 10:20.†

ἀποτομία.long: (lit: sheerness, of a rock), abruptness, harshness, severity, rigor.
ἀποτομία.as:
**† ἀποτομία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀποτέμνω, to cut of), [in Sm.: Je 51 (28):35, Na 3:1*;]
steepness, sharpness; metaph., severity (MM, s.v.): Ro 11:22.†

ἀπείθεια.as:
** ἀπείθεια
(WH, -θία, exc. He 4:6, 11), -ας, ἡ (< ἀπειθής), [in LXX IV Mac 8:9, 1812:4*;]
disobedience (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ro 11:30, 32, He 4:6, 11; υἱοὶ τῆς ἀ. (gen. of definition, v. M, Pr., 73 f.), Eph 2:25:6, Col 3:6 (T, WH, R, mg., omit).†

ἁπλότης.sd: singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal)
ἁπλότης.as:
ἀπλότης, -ητος, ή
(< ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: II Ki 15:11 (תֹּם), I Ch 29:17 (לֵבָבישֶׁר, ἁ. τῆς καρδίας, cf. Col 3:22, where v. Lft.), Wi 1:1, al.;]
simplicity, sincerity: Ro 12:8, II Co 11:3, Eph 6:5, Col 3:22; as manifested in generous, unselfish giving, liberality, graciousness: II Co 8:29:11, 13 (v. ICC, Ro., 12:8; Hort, Ja., 1:5, and v.s. ἁπλῶς).†

ἀποστυγέω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός);
ἀποστυγέω.as:
* ἀπο-στυγέω, -ῶ
(< στυγέω, to hate),
to abhor: Ro 12:9.†

ἀπόδειξις.as:
** ἀπό-δειξις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: III Mac 4:20, IV Mac 3:1913:10*;]
1.a showing off.
2. As used by Gk. philosophers, demonstration, certain proof: I Co 2:4 (v. ICC, in l.; MM, s.v.; Lft., Notes, 173).†

ἀπελεύθερος.long: a freedman, one who has been a slave but has been manumitted by his master.
ἀπελεύθερος.sd: one freed away, i.e. a freedman
ἀπελεύθερος.as:
* ἀπ-ελεύθερος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a freedman: τ. κυρίου (MM, s.v.), I Co 7:22.†

ἀπερισπάστως.der: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of G4049 (περισπάω);
ἀπερισπάστως.as:
*† ἀπερισπάστως,
adv.
(< περισπάω; the adj. occurs in Wi 16:11Si 41:1);
without distraction: I Co 7:35.†

ἀπόκριμα.der: from G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι) (in its original sense of judging);
ἀπόκριμα.as:
*† ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό
(< ἀποκρίνω);
1. prop., a judicial sentence: II Co 1:9, R, mg.
2.an answer (v. Thayer, s.v.): II Co 1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, s.v.: cf. also Cremer, 375).†

ἀπεῖπον.sd: to say off for oneself, i.e. disown
ἀπεῖπον.der: reflexive past of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G2036 (ἔπω);
ἀπεῖπον.as:
ἀπ-εῖπον, 2 aor. without present in use
[in LXX for מָאַס, אָמַר, etc.;]
1.to tell out.
2.to forbid (III Ki 11:2).
3.to renounce: 1 aor. mid. (WH, App., 164; MM, VGT, s.v.), II Co 4:2.†

ἀπαρασκεύαστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3903 (παρασκευάζω);

ἅπαξ.sd: one (or a single) time (numerically or conclusively)
ἅπαξ.as:
ἅπαξ,
adv.,
[in LXX for אֶחָד, פַּעַם;]
(a)once: II Co 11:25, He 9:26, 27; ἔτι ἅ., He 12:26, 27; ἅ. τ. ἐνιαυτοῦ, He 9:7; καί ἅ. κ. δίς, twice: Phl 4:16, I Th 2:18;
(b)once for all: He 6:49:2810:2, I Pe 3:18, Ju 3, 5 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀποτόμως.der: adverb from a derivative of a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to cut);
ἀποτόμως.as:
** ἀποτόμως,
adv.,
[in LXX: Wi 5:22*;]
abruptly, curtly, hence sharply, severely: II Co 13:10, Tit 1:13 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπαλλοτριόομαι.long: I estrange, alienate; pass: I am alienated from.
ἀπαλλοτριόομαι.sd: to estrange away, i.e. (passively and figuratively) to be non-participant
ἀπαλλοτριόομαι.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G245 (ἀλλότριος);
ἀπαλλοτριόομαι.as:
ἀπ-αλλοτριόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for זוּר, נזר, etc.;]
to alienate, estrange; pass.: Eph 2:124:18, Col 1:21 (MM, VGT, s.v.; Cremer, 95, 633).†

ἀποκαταλλάσσω.long: I reconcile, change from one state of feeling to another.
ἀποκαταλλάσσω.as:
*† ἀπο-κατ-αλλάσσω
(cf. καταλλάσσω: ἀπό here signifies completely, v. Lft., Col., 1:20, 21; Ellic., Eph., 2:16; but also Mey., Eph., 2:16),
to reconcile completely: Eph 2:16, Col 1:20, 21.†

ἀπαλγέω.g: I am past feeling, cease to care, become callous
ἀπαλγέω.long: (lit: I cease to feel [my] pain), am past feeling, cease to care (suggesting sometimes despair, sometimes recklessness), become callous, reckless.
ἀπαλγέω.sd: to grieve out, i.e. become apathetic
ἀπαλγέω.as:
* ἀπ-αλγέω, -ῶ,
1. prop., to cease to feel pain for (Thuc., ii, 61).
2. In late Gk.
(a)to despair (Polyb., i, 35, 5);
(b)to become callous, reckless (Polyb., xvi, 12, 7; MM, VGT, s.v.): Eph 4:19.†

ἀπατάω.long: I deceive, cheat, lead into error.
ἀπατάω.as:
ἀπατάω, -ῶ
(< ἀπάτη), [in LXX for פּתה, נשׁא hi., etc.;]
to deceive: c. acc., Ja 1:26; c. acc. pers., dat. rei, Eph 5:6; pass., I Ti 2:14 (on its infrequency in late writers, v. MM, VGT, s.v.; cf. ἐξαπατάω).†

ἀπουσία.as:
* ἀπουσία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἄπειμι);
1.absence (Æsch., Thuc.): Phl 2:12.
2.deficiency, waste (MM, s.v).†

ἀπέκδυσις.long: a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off.
ἀπέκδυσις.as:
*† ἀπ-έκ-δυσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀπεκδύω),
a putting or stripping off: Col 2:11 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀπεκδύομαι.sd: to divest wholly oneself, or (for oneself) despoil
ἀπεκδύομαι.der: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G1562 (ἐκδύω);
ἀπεκδύομαι.as:
*† ἀπ-εκ-δύω,
to strip off clothes or arms; mid., to strip off from oneself: Col 3:9; to strip, despoil (mid, for act., ICC, in l.; but cf. Lft., Ellic.), Col 2:15.†

ἀπόχρησις.sd: the act of using up, i.e. consumption
ἀπόχρησις.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5530 (χράομαι);
ἀπόχρησις.as:
*† ἀπό-χρησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποχράομαι, to use to the full, abuse),
abuse, misuse: Col 2:22 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπορφανίζω.g: I separate from some one, bereave
ἀπορφανίζω.long: I separate from some one, am bereaved.
ἀπορφανίζω.sd: to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse)
ἀπορφανίζω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G3737 (ὀρφανός);
ἀπορφανίζω.as:
* ἀπ-ορφανίζω
(< ἀπό, ὀρφανός),
to be bereaved (prop., of a parent, Lft., Notes, 36); metaph., I Th 2:17 (where Field thinks it = χωρισθέντες, Notes, 199).†

ἀπέραντος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of G4008 (πέραν);
ἀπέραντος.as:
ἀπέραντος, -ον
(< περαίνω, to complete, finish), [in LXX: Jb 36:26 (חֵקֶראֵין), III Mac 2:9*;]
endless, interminable: I Ti 1:4.†

ἀποδοχή.long: (properly: reception, welcome, of guests), acceptance, appreciation, approbation.
ἀποδοχή.as:
* ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἀποδέχομαι),
acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): I Ti 1:154:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, s.v.).†

ἀπόδεκτος.g: worthy to be received, acceptable, welcome
ἀπόδεκτος.long: worthy to be received (welcomed), acceptable, welcome, pleasant.

ἀπόβλητος.g: worthy to be cast away, worthless
ἀπόβλητος.long: worthy to be cast away, worthless, regarded as vile.
ἀπόβλητος.sd: cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected
ἀπόβλητος.as:
** ἀπό-βλητος, -ον
(< ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Le 7:18, al.; Sm.: Ho 9:3 (טמא);]
to be thrown away, rejected: I Ti 4:4 (Hom., Plut.).†

ἀπρόσιτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to go);
ἀπρόσιτος.as:
*† ἀ-πρόσ-ιτος, -ον
(< πρόσειμι, to go to),
unapproachable: φῶς, I Ti 6:16.†

ἀπόλαυσις.g: the faculty or experience of enjoyment
ἀπόλαυσις.long: the faculty or experience of enjoyment.
ἀπόλαυσις.der: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to enjoy);
ἀπόλαυσις.as:
** ἀπόλαυσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀπολαύω, to take of, enjoy a thing), [in LXX: III Mac 7:16*;]
enjoyment: I Ti 6:17, He 11:25 (for late exx., v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀποθησαυρίζω.as:
**† ἀπο-θησαυρίζω,
[in LXX: Si 3:4*;]
to treasure up, store away: I Ti 6:19.†

ἀπαίδευτος.long: untrained, uneducated, showing a want of training or education, ignorant.
ἀπαίδευτος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3811 (παιδεύω);
ἀπαίδευτος.as:
ἀ-παίδευτος, -ον
(< παιδεύω), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, etc., chiefly in Wi. lit.;]
uninstructed, ignorant: II Ti 2:23.†

ἀποτρέπομαι.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
ἀποτρέπομαι.as:
** ἀπο-τρέπω,
[in LXX: Si 20:2948:18, III Mac 1:23, IV Mac 1:3316:12*;]
to turn away; mid., to turn oneself away from: c. acc., II Ti 3:5.†

ἀπολείπω.g: I leave, leave behind, desert, am reserved
ἀπολείπω.long: I leave, leave behind; pass: I am reserved, remain; I desert, abandon.
ἀπολείπω.sd: to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake
ἀπολείπω.as:
ἀπο-λείπω,
[in LXX for חדליתר, etc.;]
1.to leave, leave behind (in π. a term. techn. in wills; v. MM, s.v.): II Ti 4:13, 20, Tit 1:5; pass., to be reserved, remain: He 4:6, 910:26.
2.to desert, abandon: Ju 6.†

Ἀπφία.long: Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae, either wife or sister of Philemon.

ἀποτίνω.g: I repay, pay what is due
ἀποτίνω.long: I repay, pay what is due (by way of punishment or fine), make good.
ἀποτίνω.as:
ἀπο-τίνω (or -τίω),
[in LXX chiefly for שׂלם pi.;]
to pay off, repay: Phm 19 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπαύγασμα.g: a light flashing forth, radiation, gleam
ἀπαύγασμα.long: a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam.
ἀπαύγασμα.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G826 (αὐγάζω);
ἀπαύγασμα.as:
**† ἀπ-αύγασμα, -τος, τό
(< αὐγή, brightness, whence ἀπαυγάζω, to radiate or reflect), [in LXX: Wi 7:26*;]
of light beaming from a luminous body, radiance, effulgence: He 1:3.†

ἄπειρος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3984 (πεῖρα);
ἄπειρος.as:
ἄπειρος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., πεῖρα, trial), [in LXX: Nu 14:23, Za 11:15 (אֱוִילִי), Je 2:6 (עֲרָבָה)*;]
without experience of: c. gen. rei, He 5:13 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀπάτωρ.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3962 (πατήρ);
ἀπάτωρ.as:
* ἀπάτωρ, -ορος, ὁ, ὴ
(< ἀ- neg., πατήρ);
1.fatherless.
2.without father (MM, VGT, s.v.), i.e., with no recorded genealogy: He 7:3.†

ἀπαράβατος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3845 (παραβαίνω);
ἀπαράβατος.as:
*† ἀ-παρά-βατος, -ον
(< παραβαίνω),
inviolable, and so unchangeable: He 7:24 (v. Westc., in l.; Cremer, 653; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀποβλέπω.g: I look away from, turn my attention to
ἀποβλέπω.long: I look away from all else at one object, look steadfastly.
ἀποβλέπω.sd: to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard
ἀποβλέπω.as:
ἀπο-βλέπω,
[in LXX for פּנה, etc.;]
to look away from all else at one object; hence, to look steadfastly: He 11:26 (cf. ἀφοράω).†

ἁπλῶς.der: adverb from G573 (ἁπλοῦς) (in the objective sense of G572 (ἁπλότης));
ἁπλῶς.as:
ἁπλῶς,
adv.
(< ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: Pr 10:9 (בַּתֹּם), Wi 16:27, II Mac 6:6*;]
simply, sincerely, graciously: Ja 1:5. ("Later writers comprehend under the one word the whole magnanimous and honourable type of character in which ... singleness of mind is the central feature"—Hort, Ja., 1:5)†

ἀπείραστος.g: untried, inexperienced, incapable of being tempted
ἀπείραστος.long: untried, inexperienced, untempted, incapable of being tempted.
ἀπείραστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3987 (πειράω);
ἀπείραστος.as:
*† ἀπείραστος, -ον
(< πειράζω; for cl. ἀπείρητος, < πειράω),
untempted, untried, without experience: Ja 1:13 (v. Hort, in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀποκυέω.g: I bring forth, give birth to
ἀποκυέω.long: I bring forth, give birth to (a child), a medical or physical word, marking the close of pregnancy.
ἀποκυέω.sd: to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively)
ἀποκυέω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2949 (κῦμα);
ἀποκυέω.as:
** ἀπο-κυέω (Rec. -κύω), -ῶ
(< ἀπό, κυέω or κύω, to be pregnant), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:17*;]
prop., "the medical word for birth as the close of pregnancy" (Hort, Ja., 26 f.). In κοινή, "an ordinary syn. of τίκτω, but definitely 'perfectivised' (M, Pr., 111 ff.; MM, s.v.) by the ἀπό, and so implying safe delivery," to bring forth, give birth to: Ja 1:15, 18.†

ἀποσκίασμα.g: a shadow, a faint image or copy
ἀποσκίασμα.long: either a shadow cast by an object, or a faint image or copy of an object.
ἀποσκίασμα.der: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά);
ἀποσκίασμα.as:
*† ἀπο-σκίασμα, -τος, τό
(< ἀποσκιάζω, to cast a shadow; v.s. σκία),
a shadow: Ja 1:17 (MM, s.v.).†

ἀπροσωπολήμπτως.long: (literary and Jewish), without any preference (undue favor, partiality) for a person.
ἀπροσωπολήμπτως.sd: in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially
ἀπροσωπολήμπτως.der: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of G4383 (πρόσωπον) and G2983 (λαμβάνω) (compare G4381 (προσωπολήπτης));
ἀπροσωπολήμπτως.as:
*† ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (Rec. -λήπτως, cl.),
adv.
(< α- neg., προσωπολήμπτης),
without respect of persons, impartially: I Pe 1:17.†

ἀπογίνομαι.g: I go out of being, cease to be, die
ἀπογίνομαι.long: I am away, am removed from, depart life, die.
ἀπογίνομαι.der: past participle of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1096 (γίνομαι);
ἀπογίνομαι.as:
** ἀπο-γίνομαι (cl. -γίγν-)
[in LXX: Da TH 2:1*;]
1.to be away, removed from.
2.to depart life, to die (MM, s.v.): τ. ἁμαρτίαις, i.e. with ref. to sins, I Pe 2:24 (Cremer, 149, 668).†

ἀπονέμω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);
ἀπονέμω.as:
ἀπο-νέμω
(< νέμω, to distribute), [in LXX: De 4:19 (חלק), III Mac 1:73:16*;]
to assign, apportion: I Pe 3:7. (In π. of a Prefect who renders to all their dues; v. MM, s.v.)†

ἀπόθεσις.g: a putting off, a laying down
ἀπόθεσις.long: a putting off, a laying down.
ἀπόθεσις.as:
* ἀπό-θεσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἀποτίθημι),
a putting away: I Pe 3:21, II Pe 1:14.†

ἀποφεύγω.as:
** ἀπο-φεύγω,
[in LXX: Si 22:22*;]
to flee from, escape: c. acc., II Pe 2:18, 20; c. gen., II Pe 1:4.†

ἀποδιορίζω.long: I make a logical distinction, make an invidious distinction.
ἀποδιορίζω.sd: to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party)
ἀποδιορίζω.der: from G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of G223 (Ἀλέξανδρος) and G3724 (ὁρίζω);
ἀποδιορίζω.as:
* ἀπο-δι-ορίζω
(< διορίζω, < ἅρος, a limit),
to mark off, hence metaph. to make separations: Ju 19 (Cremer, 806).†

ἄπταιστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4417 (πταίω);
ἄπταιστος.as:
** ἄ-πταιστος, -ον
(< πταίω), [in LXX: III Mac 6:39*;]
without stumbling, sure-footed: metaph. (MM, s.v.), Ju 24.†

Ἀπολλύων.long: Apollyon, The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebrew: Abaddon.
Ἀπολλύων.as:
Ἀπολλύων, -οντος, ὁ
(pres. ptcp. of ἀπολλύω),
Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Re 9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.)†
